$$
{u}^{′}(x)=2x,\,{v}^{′}(x)=6\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x+5).
$$

Note that we used the chain rule to differentiate $v.$

Now, applying the product rule and simplifying, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & =(2x)(\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x+5))+({x}^{2})(6\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x+5)) \\  & =2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x+5)+6{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x+5).\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["d6c704d0-15db-517b-aa14-8aa5c95b21ff"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "generator" :question-generator/id #uuid "c8ef6baf-f8d3-5c68-84d8-ed19f665eb6d" :question-generator/script "generate/scratch/17592186096845.py"} [:db/add 17592186096845 :knowledge-point/question-generator "generator"] {:db/id 17592186096845 :knowledge-point/questions ["13151117-2915-58a7-8af2-4dc4a9478503"]} [:db/ensure 17592186096845 :knowledge-point/validate]]
